# Index funds

Where the long-term money lives and why. Rewritten Feb 2025 after the platform move, because the old version still talked about Hargreaves Lansdown and I kept confusing myself.

## The core holding

One fund does most of the work: **Vanguard FTSE Global All Cap Index**, accumulation units, OCF 0.23%. Roughly 7,300 companies across developed and emerging markets, small caps included. I looked at the plain FTSE All-World (0.22%) and honestly the difference is noise, but All Cap goes down into the small companies and I like that.

Balance in the Stocks and Shares ISA on 10 Feb 2025: £41,862.17. Contributions so far this tax year: £14,400 (£1,200 a month by standing order on the 3rd, one day after invoices usually clear).

The rest of the ISA:

- 10% Vanguard UK Gilt UCITS ETF (VGOV), mainly so I have something to rebalance from when equities drop
- nothing else. I sold the Fundsmith Equity holding in 2023 at 1.04% OCF, see below

## Why passive, in one paragraph

I spend all day looking at other people's books. I have no edge picking companies and I know it. Every active fund I've held for more than three years has lagged its benchmark after fees: Fundsmith by about 4.1% a year over 2021 to 2023, Baillie Gifford American by a lot more than that (that one I'd rather not think about). A tracker guarantees I get the market minus a tiny fee, and I'm fine with average.

## Platform switch, March 2024

Moved from Hargreaves Lansdown to Vanguard Investor. Transfer reference VG-TRF-552081, requested 4 March 2024, completed 2 April 2024. Done as an in-specie transfer so I was never out of the market, and it kept the ISA wrapper intact.

Fee maths that made the decision for me:

| | HL | Vanguard Investor |
|---|---|---|
| Platform fee | 0.45% | 0.15% |
| Cap | none on funds | £375 a year |
| On £38k | ~£171 | £57 |

£114 a year saved, more as the pot grows. The HL app is nicer. Not £114 nicer.

## Rebalancing rule

Once a year, first week of April, after the new ISA allowance opens. If the gilt ETF is outside 7% to 13% I put that year's new money into whichever side is light rather than selling anything. I've only had to actually sell once (April 2022, sold £1,900 of global equity). Written down so I don't fiddle with it in between.

## Kids' Junior ISAs

- Isla (born 2015): JISA at Vanguard, same All Cap fund, £100 a month. £8,914 on 10 Feb 2025.
- Theo (born 2018): opened Sept 2023, £75 a month plus whatever grandma sends at Christmas. £2,780.

Both locked until 18, which is the point. Isla doesn't know the number and I intend to keep it that way for a long time.

## Things I keep getting wrong

- Accumulation vs income units. I hold **accumulation** in the ISA. The dividends get rolled back into the unit price, so there's no separate payment to reinvest. The income-unit situation in the general account is a different beast, see [[Dividend reinvestment]].
- Tracking difference is not the same as OCF. The All Cap fund trailed its index by 0.31% in 2024, not 0.23%. Check the factsheet, not the headline figure.
- Don't check the balance in a bad week. I did in August 2024 (the yen carry thing) and spent an evening reading forums. Pointless.
